summary.name: LLMStack
summary.one_liner: LLMStack's blog post explaining retrieval augmented generation (RAG): what it is, how its data preparation, retrieval and generation stages work, and how RAG is built into LLMStack.
use_cases: understanding how RAG improves LLM answers
designing a chunking and embedding pipeline
summary.what_it_does: The page is a long explainer on retrieval augmented generation. It describes RAG as passing relevant retrieved information to an LLM with the question, and compares it with fine-tuning. It walks through three stages (data preparation, retrieval, generation) and covers vector stores, keyword search, graph databases and search engines as data sources. It lists techniques for improving RAG such as hybrid search, summaries, overlapping chunks, fine-tuned embeddings, metadata, re-ranking and reordering for the lost-in-the-middle problem. It ends with a section on how RAG is built into LLMStack, where creating a datasource handles chunking and embeddings automatically.
notable: Covers hybrid search, overlapping chunks, re-ranking and the lost-in-the-middle problem
Explains how LLMStack handles RAG out of the box via datasources and Text-Chat processors
Mentions templates such as Website Chatbot and AI Augmented Search that use RAG
caveats: Page is an educational article; it does not describe pricing for LLMStack
Mentions a cloud offering (Promptly) without stating its terms
